title: Criteria for Inclusion of Medical Specialists into Insurer's Panel for Integrated Shield Plans
what_it_is: Criteria for Inclusion of Medical Specialists into Insurer's Panel for Integrated Shield Plans

sections.label: Questions on Integrated Shield Plans
sections.summary: Questions to the Minister for Health cover panel criteria, premium increases, review timeline, anti-competition, switching doctors, Singaporeans relinquishing plans, and overseas regulation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health with regard to the Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee (a) whether it will be made transparent to the public, the criteria for inclusion of specialists into an insurer's panel for its Integrated Shield Plans; (b) whether there will be a more controlled rate of premium increase for such plans to safeguard the public's ability to sustain such plans as they age; and (c) what is the expected timeline for the Committee to complete its review and recommendations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) whether empanelling of specialist doctors for Integrated Shield Plans will result in anti-competition; and (b) whether the Ministry has considered the possible impact on patients having to switch doctors mid-treatment due to this practice of empanelling doctors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health (a) over the last five years how many Singaporeans relinquished an existing Integrated Shield Plan; and (b) what is their median age; and (c) of the above, how many did not later purchase a new Integrated Shield Plan and how many were subsequently admitted to public hospitals.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry has studied the regulation of private health insurance in overseas jurisdictions and the possible learning points for Singapore, in particular the feasibility and implications of requiring Integrated Shield Plan (IP) insurers to accept policyholders intending or forced to switch from another IP provider, such that existing covered conditions are not permanently excluded from future coverage.

sections.label: Integrated Shield Plan distribution
sections.summary: Less than 1% of Singapore residents have a Standard IP plan, 10% class B1, 20% class A, and 40% private hospital IP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Currently, less than 1% of Singapore residents have a Standard IP plan, 10% have a class B1 IP, 20% have a class A IP and 40% have a private hospital IP.

sections.label: Private hospital bill growth
sections.summary: Between 2007 and 2019, private hospital bills among IP cases grew at 4%, twice as fast as unsubsidised public healthcare bills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Between 2007 and 2019, private hospital bills among IP cases grew at 4%, twice as fast as unsubsidised bills in public healthcare institutions.

sections.label: Minimum co-payment for riders
sections.summary: MOH introduced a minimum 5% co-payment for all new private riders in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: MOH, therefore, introduced a minimum 5% co-payment for all new private riders in 2018.

sections.label: Co-payment cap for panelled doctors
sections.summary: MOH allowed insurers to apply a $3,000 co-payment cap for treatment from panelled doctors with negotiated fee arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To provide some assurance to policyholders who were concerned with potentially large co-payments, MOH therefore allowed insurers to apply a $3,000 co-payment cap for treatment from panelled doctors with negotiated fee arrangements with insurers.

sections.label: Growth of insurer panels
sections.summary: MOH encouraged insurers to grow panels; some increased specialists by over 40% since August 2019, and over 70% of private specialists are on at least one IP panel.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To address this, MOH has encouraged all insurers to grow the size of their panels and some have already increased the number of specialists on their panels by more than 40% since August 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Today, more than 70% of private specialists are on at least one IP panel.

sections.label: Pre-authorisation and co-payment caps
sections.summary: Pre-authorisation minimises runaway bill sizes, and some insurers have extended the co-payment cap to pre-authorised claims by non-panel doctors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: With pre-authorisation, the risk of runaway bill sizes would then be minimised.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Hence, some insurers have extended the co-payment cap to pre-authorised claims for treatment by non-panel doctors to provide policyholders with greater assurance, and we certainly encourage more to do so.

sections.label: Study of portable IP insurance
sections.summary: MOH will study whether IP insurance can be made fully portable, including looking at examples abroad.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: MOH will study whether IP insurance can be made fully portable, including looking at examples abroad.

sections.label: MAS oversight of insurers
sections.summary: MAS exercises regulatory oversight over insurers' financial standing, risk management and governance so they can meet obligations to policyholders.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To ensure that insurers remain financially sound and are able to meet their obligations to policyholders, MAS exercises regulatory oversight over the insurers' financial standing, risk management and governance.

sections.label: Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee appointed
sections.summary: MOH appointed a 12-member Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee in April this year to provide a platform on health insurance issues.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: To support these efforts, MOH appointed a 12-member Multilateral Healthcare Insurance Committee (MHIC) in April this year to provide a platform for healthcare providers, payers, consumer representatives and the Government to work on these issues related to health insurance.

sections.label: Four areas of committee work
sections.summary: The four areas are panels and pre-authorisation, transparency, a claims complaints process, and a patient and consumer-centric viewpoint.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: First, panels and pre-authorisation, including streamlining the processes I spoke about earlier; second, issues pertaining to improving transparency across the board, including providing more detailed and itemised information about healthcare bills and publishing data on claims and premiums, so that insurers, providers and policyholders can make better informed decisions; third, establishing a claims complaints process supported by AMS and LIA so that stakeholders have an avenue for recourse should they feel unfairly treated, such as where insurers or patients may wish to raise concerns about over-servicing or over-charging, or if doctors have concerns about certain insurer practices; and, fourth, examining the issues from a patient and consumer-centric viewpoint to ensure that the patient and public interests are best safeguarded.

sections.label: Committee's first meeting
sections.summary: The Committee has already begun its work with the first meeting held on 27 April.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Committee has already begun its work with the first meeting held on 27 April.

sections.label: Claims Complaints Panel setup
sections.summary: A Claims Complaints Panel comprising insurers and the Academy of Medicine of Singapore will be set up to provide independence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The second issue on independent assessment, as Members have heard from my reply earlier, we will be setting up a Claims Complaints Panel that comprises the insurers plus also the Academy of Medicine of Singapore who are specialists in the respective fields.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, that provides some degree of independence from the professional side or of both the stakeholders to really look at any areas, whether it is insurers or doctors, which have got some unhappiness over the way payments are done or the way a certain case is being assessed by either party.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So, yes, there will be an independent panel that is going to be in the works.

sections.label: Patient access to doctors
sections.summary: The key is ensuring patients have access to any doctor they want, with pre-authorisation as the better way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think the more important way to look at this is how can we make sure that care is accessible to our patients, whether the mechanism is empanelment or otherwise?

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think the key is to make sure patients have access to any doctor they want to see, which is why I think the better way to go for is to look at pre-authorisation.

sections.label: Transparent insurer pricing information
sections.summary: Information on how each insurer prices its policies and its benefits should be transparent for comparison.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In terms of ranking of insurers, I think what is important is to have information on how each insurer price its policies and what benefits it has transparently so that patients or policyholders themselves can make a comparison and take a look.

sections.label: FIDReC dispute mechanism
sections.summary: FIDReC already has a mechanism to address policyholder concerns on policy terms or unfair treatment by an insurer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Actually today, FIDReC, the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre already has a mechanism in place to address any policyholder's concerns pertaining to whether it is policy terms or unfair treatment by an insurer.

sections.label: Insurer failure and PPF Scheme
sections.summary: A liquidator must try to sell or transfer the insurance business, and the PPF Scheme covers policies including IP plans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: If an insurer fails and undergoes winding up processes under the Insurance Act, the appointed liquidator is required to endeavour as far as possible, and reasonably practicable to sell, or transfer the whole or part of the insurance business to another insurer before considering other options.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Policyowners' Protection Scheme, or PPF Scheme, is also in place which aims to provide coverage for policies which are commonly purchased by consumers, and/or cause significant impact of destruction to policyholders should the insurer fail.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This would include accident and health policies such as IP plans, which will be fully covered under the PPF scheme, in an event that the insurer fails.

sections.label: MediShield Life and pre-authorisation
sections.summary: MediShield Life covers all pre-existing conditions for life, and MHIC prioritises expanding and streamlining pre-authorisation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Should all else fail, MediShield Life will be here to cover you universally with no exclusion on all your pre-existing conditions for life.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Which is why in one of the work streams that the MHIC endeavours to do, as one of their earliest priorities, is to look at how they can further expand and streamline the pre-authorisation process.

sections.label: Access to non-panel doctors
sections.summary: The passage states that IP-insured patients can access non-panel doctors through pre-authorisation, noting differences in benefits between panel and non-panel doctors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The difference, of course, is in some of the benefits of panel and non-panel doctors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: But today, any IP-insured patient can actually have access to non-panel doctors through pre-authorisation.

sections.label: Publishing information on websites
sections.summary: The passage states that as much information as possible will be put on the MOH website and the LIA website.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: I think the second question is easier to answer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will just put as much information as possible, whether it is on MOH website, whether it is on the LIA website.
